title: IIT JAM 2027 Physics (PH) — Full Length Mock Test 04
titleEn: IIT JAM 2027 Physics (PH) — Full Length Mock Test 04

questions.questionTextEn: An infinite flat conducting sheet lying in the $xy$-plane carries a uniform surface current density $\vec{K} = K_0\hat{x}$. The magnetic field in the region $z > 0$ is
questions.explanationEn: By Ampère's law and the right-hand rule for $\vec{K} = K_0\hat{x}$, the magnetic field is uniform with magnitude $\frac{\mu_0 K_0}{2}$, pointing along $-\hat{y}$ for $z > 0$ and $+\hat{y}$ for $z < 0$.

questions.questionTextEn: If $Q$ is an $n \times n$ real orthogonal matrix, which one of the following statements is ALWAYS true?
questions.explanationEn: By definition, a real orthogonal matrix satisfies $Q^T Q = I$, so $Q^{-1} = Q^T$. Taking determinants gives $(\det Q)^2 = 1 \implies \det(Q) = \pm 1$. Proper rotations have $\det = +1$ and improper reflections have $\det = -1$, while eigenvalues can be complex on the unit circle. Hence, option (C) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: In Compton scattering of a photon off a stationary free electron, the kinetic energy imparted to the recoiling electron is maximum when the photon scattering angle $\theta$ is:
questions.explanationEn: The photon wavelength shift $\Delta\lambda = \frac{h}{m_e c}(1 - \cos\theta)$ is maximum at $\theta = 180^\circ$ (backscattering), where the scattered photon loses the maximum possible energy, transferring the maximum kinetic energy to the recoiling electron. Hence, option (B) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: If the acoustic intensity of a sound wave increases by a factor of $1000$, the corresponding increase in sound intensity level in decibels ($\text{dB}$) is
questions.explanationEn: The change in sound level is $\Delta\beta = 10\log_{10}\left(\frac{I_2}{I_1}\right) = 10\log_{10}(10^3) = 30\text{ dB}$.

questions.questionTextEn: A conducting surface in vacuum carries a local surface charge density $\sigma$. The outward electrostatic pressure (force per unit area) acting on the surface of the conductor is
questions.explanationEn: Just outside the conductor $E = \sigma/\varepsilon_0$ and inside $E = 0$, so the average field acting on the surface charge itself is $E_{\text{avg}} = \frac{\sigma}{2\varepsilon_0}$. The outward pressure is $P = \sigma E_{\text{avg}} = \frac{\sigma^2}{2\varepsilon_0}$.

questions.questionTextEn: In elementary kinetic theory, the thermal conductivity $K$ of a dilute ideal gas of fixed molecular species at constant temperature $T$ depends on the gas pressure $P$ as:
questions.explanationEn: Thermal conductivity is $K = \frac{1}{3} n c_v \bar{v} \lambda$, where $c_v$ is molecular heat capacity. Because $\lambda \propto 1/n$, the product $n\lambda$ is independent of $n$ (and hence independent of $P$ at fixed $T$). Thus $K$ is independent of $P$. Hence, option (A) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: A viscous liquid flows steadily in laminar regime through a horizontal capillary tube of radius $R$ under a fixed pressure difference. If the tube is replaced by another tube of the same length but radius $R/2$ under the same pressure difference, the volume flow rate changes by a factor of
questions.explanationEn: By Poiseuille's law, $Q = \frac{\pi \Delta P R^4}{8\eta L} \propto R^4$. Halving the radius reduces $Q$ by a factor of $(1/2)^4 = \frac{1}{16}$. Hence, option (A) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: The commutator $[\hat{x}^2, \hat{p}_x]$ between the squared position operator $\hat{x}^2$ and the momentum operator $\hat{p}_x = -i\hbar\frac{d}{dx}$ is:
questions.explanationEn: Using $[AB, C] = A[B, C] + [A, C]B$ and $[\hat{x}, \hat{p}_x] = i\hbar$: $[\hat{x}^2, \hat{p}_x] = \hat{x}[\hat{x}, \hat{p}_x] + [\hat{x}, \hat{p}_x]\hat{x} = i\hbar\hat{x} + i\hbar\hat{x} = 2i\hbar\hat{x}$. Hence, option (B) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: A sinusoidal voltage $v_{\text{in}}(t) = 10\sin(\omega t)\text{ V}$ is applied to an ideal clamping circuit consisting of a capacitor $C$ in series with the input and an ideal diode connected across the output with its anode grounded and cathode connected to the output node (and a very large parallel load resistor $R$ such that $RC \gg 2\pi/\omega$). In steady state, the output voltage $v_{\text{out}}(t)$ swings between:
questions.explanationEn: During the negative half-cycle when $v_{\text{in}}$ reaches $-10\text{ V}$, the ideal diode (anode grounded, cathode at output) becomes forward-biased and clamps $v_{\text{out}} = 0\text{ V}$, charging the capacitor to $+10\text{ V}$ (with the right plate positive relative to the left plate). Because $RC \gg T$, the capacitor holds this $10\text{ V}$ DC offset, so $v_{\text{out}}(t) = v_{\text{in}}(t) + 10\text{ V} = 10 + 10\sin(\omega t)\text{ V}$, which swings between $0\text{ V}$ and $+20\text{ V}$. Hence, the correct option is (B).

questions.questionTextEn: The outward flux of the vector field $\vec{F} = 2x\hat{i} + 3y\hat{j} - z\hat{k}$ through a closed spherical surface of radius $R$ centered at the origin is
questions.explanationEn: By the Gauss divergence theorem, $\oint_S \vec{F}\cdot d\vec{S} = \iiint_V (\nabla\cdot\vec{F})\,dV$. Here $\nabla\cdot\vec{F} = 2 + 3 - 1 = 4$. Thus, the flux is $4 \times \frac{4}{3}\pi R^3 = \frac{16}{3}\pi R^3$. Hence, option (D) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: A symmetric triangular voltage waveform of frequency $f$ is applied to the input of an ideal inverting Op-Amp differentiator (input capacitor $C$ connected to the inverting terminal, feedback resistor $R$ between output and inverting terminal, non-inverting terminal grounded). Assuming the Op-Amp does not saturate, the output voltage waveform is a:
questions.explanationEn: For an ideal inverting Op-Amp differentiator, $V_o(t) = -RC \frac{dV_{\text{in}}}{dt}$. A symmetric triangular wave has a constant positive slope during one half-cycle (producing a constant negative output) and a constant negative slope during the other half-cycle (producing a constant positive output). Thus, the output is a square wave of the same frequency $f$. Hence, the correct option is (B).

questions.questionTextEn: At $T = 0\text{ K}$, the ratio of the average kinetic energy per electron in a three-dimensional free electron gas to its Fermi energy $E_F$ is $r_3$, and the corresponding ratio in a two-dimensional free electron gas is $r_2$. The values of $r_3$ and $r_2$ are, respectively:
questions.explanationEn: In $d$ dimensions, the free-electron density of states scales as $g(E) \propto E^{d/2 - 1}$. Thus, at $T = 0\text{ K}$, $\langle E \rangle = \frac{\int_0^{E_F} E \cdot E^{d/2 - 1}\,dE}{\int_0^{E_F} E^{d/2 - 1}\,dE} = \frac{d/2}{d/2 + 1} E_F = \frac{d}{d + 2} E_F$. For $d = 3$, $r_3 = \frac{3}{5}$; for $d = 2$, $r_2 = \frac{2}{4} = \frac{1}{2}$. Hence, the correct option is (A).

questions.questionTextEn: A one-dimensional quantum harmonic oscillator of angular frequency $\omega$ has energy levels $E_n = \left(n + \frac{1}{2}\right)\hbar\omega$ ($n = 0, 1, 2, \dots$). In thermal equilibrium at temperature $T$ (with $\beta = \frac{1}{k_B T}$), its mean energy $\langle E \rangle$ is:
questions.explanationEn: The partition function is $Z = \sum_{n=0}^\infty e^{-\beta(n+1/2)\hbar\omega} = \frac{e^{-\beta\hbar\omega/2}}{1 - e^{-\beta\hbar\omega}} = \frac{1}{2\sinh(\beta\hbar\omega/2)}$. Differentiating gives $\langle E \rangle = -\frac{\partial \ln Z}{\partial \beta} = \frac{\hbar\omega}{2}\coth\left(\frac{\beta\hbar\omega}{2}\right)$. Hence, option (C) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: In a Young's double-slit experiment using monochromatic light of wavelength $600\text{ nm}$, a thin transparent sheet of thickness $6\ \mu\text{m}$ and refractive index $1.5$ is placed over one of the slits. The central bright fringe shifts by
questions.explanationEn: Inserting the slab adds an optical path difference $\Delta = (n - 1)t = (1.5 - 1)(6 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m}) = 3 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m}$. The shift in units of fringe width is $N = \frac{\Delta}{\lambda} = \frac{3 \times 10^{-6}}{6 \times 10^{-7}} = 5$ fringe widths.

questions.questionTextEn: A quantum particle is confined to a two-dimensional rectangular infinite potential well of dimensions $L_x = L$ and $L_y = 2L$. Defining $E_0 = \frac{\pi^2 \hbar^2}{2mL^2}$, the lowest energy level that exhibits degeneracy is:
questions.explanationEn: The energy eigenvalues are $E(n_x, n_y) = E_0\left(n_x^2 + \frac{n_y^2}{4}\right)$. Listing states in increasing order: $(1,1) \to 1.25E_0$, $(1,2) \to 2E_0$, $(1,3) \to 3.25E_0$, $(2,1) \to 4.25E_0$, and both $(2,2)$ and $(1,4)$ give $2^2 + \frac{2^2}{4} = 1^2 + \frac{4^2}{4} = 5E_0$. Thus $5E_0$ is the lowest degenerate level. Hence, option (C) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: A straight frictionless tunnel is dug along a chord of a uniform spherical planet of mass $M$ and radius $R$ at a perpendicular distance $R/2$ from the planet's center. A particle released from rest at one end of the tunnel executes simple harmonic motion with time period
questions.explanationEn: At coordinate $x$ along the chord from its midpoint, the radial distance is $r = \sqrt{x^2 + (R/2)^2}$. The component of the interior gravitational force $F = -\frac{GMm}{R^3}r$ along the chord is $F_x = -\frac{GMm}{R^3}r\left(\frac{x}{r}\right) = -\frac{GMm}{R^3}x$, independent of the chord's offset! Thus $\omega = \sqrt{\frac{GM}{R^3}}$ and $T = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{R^3}{GM}}$. Hence, option (B) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: A tightly wound toroidal coil has $N$ total turns carrying steady current $I$, with inner radius $a$ and outer radius $b$. Inside the core of the toroid at radial distance $r$ ($a < r < b$) from the symmetry axis, the magnitude of the magnetic field is
questions.explanationEn: Applying Ampère's law to a circular loop of radius $r$ ($a < r < b$) concentric with the toroid axis encloses all $N$ turns carrying current $I$: $B(2\pi r) = \mu_0 N I \implies B(r) = \frac{\mu_0 N I}{2\pi r}$.

questions.questionTextEn: For a particle in the ground state ($n = 1$) of a one-dimensional infinite square well spanning $0 \le x \le L$, the expectation value $\langle x^2 \rangle$ is:
questions.explanationEn: Evaluating $\langle x^2 \rangle = \frac{2}{L}\int_0^L x^2 \sin^2\left(\frac{\pi x}{L}\right)dx = \frac{1}{L}\int_0^L x^2\left[1 - \cos\left(\frac{2\pi x}{L}\right)\right]dx = L^2\left(\frac{1}{3} - \frac{1}{2\pi^2}\right)$. Hence, option (A) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: The center of mass of a uniform solid right circular cone of height $H$ and base radius $R$ lies on its symmetry axis at a height above the circular base equal to
questions.explanationEn: Measuring $z$ downward from the apex ($0 \le z \le H$), $z_{\text{cm}} = \frac{\int_0^H z \cdot \pi(Rz/H)^2 dz}{\int_0^H \pi(Rz/H)^2 dz} = \frac{H^4/4}{H^3/3} = \frac{3H}{4}$. Therefore, its height above the circular base is $H - \frac{3H}{4} = \frac{H}{4}$. Hence, option (C) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: For the Pauli matrix $\sigma_x = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}$ and a real parameter $\theta$, the matrix exponential $e^{i\theta\sigma_x}$ equals
questions.explanationEn: Since $\sigma_x^2 = I$, separating even and odd powers in $e^{i\theta\sigma_x} = \sum_{k=0}^\infty \frac{(i\theta)^k}{k!}\sigma_x^k$ gives $e^{i\theta\sigma_x} = I\cos\theta + i\sigma_x\sin\theta = \begin{pmatrix} \cos\theta & i\sin\theta \\ i\sin\theta & \cos\theta \end{pmatrix}$. Hence, option (D) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: A thin plano-convex lens of refractive index $n = 1.5$ and radius of curvature $R = 30\text{ cm}$ is silvered on its flat surface. The system acts as a concave mirror of focal length
questions.explanationEn: The focal length of the plano-convex lens is $f_L = \frac{R}{n - 1} = \frac{30}{0.5} = 60\text{ cm}$, and the flat silvered surface has $f_m = \infty$. The equivalent mirror power is $P_{\text{eq}} = \frac{2}{f_L} + \frac{1}{f_m} = \frac{2}{60} = \frac{1}{30}\text{ cm}^{-1}$, so it acts as a concave mirror of focal length $30\text{ cm}$.

questions.questionTextEn: A particle executes bounded periodic motion in a central potential $V(r) = c r^4$ ($c > 0$). By the virial theorem, the ratio of the time-averaged kinetic energy $\langle T \rangle$ to the total mechanical energy $E$ is
questions.explanationEn: For a homogeneous potential $V(r) \propto r^n$, the virial theorem states $\langle T \rangle = \frac{n}{2}\langle V \rangle$. With $n = 4$, $\langle T \rangle = 2\langle V \rangle$, so $E = \langle T \rangle + \langle V \rangle = \frac{3}{2}\langle T \rangle \implies \frac{\langle T \rangle}{E} = \frac{2}{3}$. Hence, option (B) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: A solid non-conducting sphere of radius $R$ has a uniform volume charge density $\rho$. A spherical cavity of radius $r_c < R/2$ is carved out inside it, with the center of the cavity displaced by a vector $\vec{a}$ from the center of the sphere. The electric field at any point inside the cavity is
optionsEn: identically zero everywhere inside the cavity
radial from the cavity center with magnitude $\frac{\rho r}{3\varepsilon_0}$
questions.explanationEn: By superposition, the sphere with a cavity equals a full sphere of density $+\rho$ centered at $\vec{0}$ plus a smaller sphere of density $-\rho$ centered at $\vec{a}$. At any point $\vec{r}$ inside the cavity, $\vec{E} = \frac{\rho\vec{r}}{3\varepsilon_0} + \frac{(-\rho)(\vec{r} - \vec{a})}{3\varepsilon_0} = \frac{\rho\vec{a}}{3\varepsilon_0}$, which is completely uniform.

questions.questionTextEn: Under the coordinate transformation $x = u(1 - v)$ and $y = uv$, the Jacobian determinant $\frac{\partial(x, y)}{\partial(u, v)}$ is equal to
questions.explanationEn: Computing the partial derivatives gives $\frac{\partial(x, y)}{\partial(u, v)} = \begin{vmatrix} 1 - v & -u \\ v & u \end{vmatrix} = u(1 - v) - (-uv) = u$. Hence, option (A) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: An ideal gas is maintained at temperature $T$ inside a chamber with a pinhole whose diameter is much smaller than the mean free path. The average translational kinetic energy of the molecules effusing out through the pinhole is:
questions.explanationEn: The effusion rate of molecules with speed $v$ is proportional to $v f(v) \propto v^3 e^{-mv^2/(2k_B T)}$, biasing the escaping beam toward faster molecules. The average kinetic energy is $\langle K \rangle_{\text{eff}} = \frac{\int_0^\infty (\frac{1}{2}mv^2) v^3 e^{-mv^2/(2k_B T)}\,dv}{\int_0^\infty v^3 e^{-mv^2/(2k_B T)}\,dv} = 2k_B T$. Hence, option (B) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: A relativistic particle of rest mass $m$ moves along the $x$-axis with instantaneous speed $v$ (Lorentz factor $\gamma = (1 - v^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$). A force $\vec{F}$ is applied parallel to its velocity. The instantaneous acceleration $a$ of the particle is:
questions.explanationEn: Differentiating $p = \gamma m v$ with respect to time gives $F = \frac{dp}{dt} = m\left(\gamma + v\frac{d\gamma}{dv}\right)a = m\left(\gamma + \gamma^3\frac{v^2}{c^2}\right)a = \gamma^3 m a$. Thus $a = \frac{F}{\gamma^3 m}$. Hence, option (B) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: An integrating factor that converts the inexact differential equation $(3xy + y^2)\,dx + (x^2 + xy)\,dy = 0$ into an exact differential equation is
questions.explanationEn: With $M = 3xy + y^2$ and $N = x^2 + xy$, we compute $\frac{1}{N}\left(\frac{\partial M}{\partial y} - \frac{\partial N}{\partial x}\right) = \frac{(3x + 2y) - (2x + y)}{x(x + y)} = \frac{x + y}{x(x + y)} = \frac{1}{x}$. Since this depends only on $x$, an integrating factor is $\mu(x) = \exp\left(\int \frac{1}{x}\,dx\right) = x$. Hence, option (D) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: Consider a system of $N$ non-interacting, localized spin-$1/2$ paramagnetic atoms, each with magnetic moment $\mu$, placed in a uniform magnetic field $B$ at temperature $T$. Letting $x = \frac{\mu B}{k_B T}$, the magnetic heat capacity at constant field $C_B$ is:
questions.explanationEn: The single-spin partition function is $Z_1 = e^x + e^{-x} = 2\cosh x$, giving mean energy $U = -N\mu B\tanh x$. Differentiating with respect to $T$ at constant $B$ using $\frac{dx}{dT} = -\frac{x}{T}$ yields $C_B = \left(\frac{\partial U}{\partial T}\right)_B = -N\mu B \operatorname{sech}^2(x)\left(-\frac{x}{T}\right) = Nk_B x^2 \operatorname{sech}^2(x)$. Hence, option (B) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: Two identical blocks, each of mass $m$, rest on a frictionless horizontal track. Each block is attached to a fixed wall by a spring of force constant $k$, and the two blocks are connected to each other by a central spring of force constant $3k$. The ratio of the higher normal-mode angular frequency to the lower normal-mode angular frequency is
questions.explanationEn: In the symmetric (in-phase) mode, the middle spring is unstretched, so $\omega_1 = \sqrt{k/m}$. In the antisymmetric (out-of-phase) mode, the midpoint of the central spring is fixed (halving its length and doubling its stiffness to $6k$), giving $\omega_2 = \sqrt{(k + 2(3k))/m} = \sqrt{7k/m}$. Thus $\omega_2 / \omega_1 = \sqrt{7}$.

questions.questionTextEn: The minimal sum-of-products (SOP) form of the Boolean function $F(A, B, C) = AB + \bar{A}C + BC$ is:
questions.explanationEn: By the consensus theorem, the term $BC$ is redundant: $BC = (A + \bar{A})BC = ABC + \bar{A}BC$. Substituting into $F$ gives $F = AB(1 + C) + \bar{A}C(1 + B) = AB + \bar{A}C$. Hence, the correct option is (B).

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following definite integrals has/have the value $\sqrt{\pi}$?
questions.explanationEn: (B) Standard Gaussian integral equals $\sqrt{\pi}$. (A) $\Gamma(1/2) = \sqrt{\pi}$ (substituting $t = x^2$ gives $2\int_0^\infty e^{-x^2}\,dx = \sqrt{\pi}$). (C) Using $\int_0^\infty x^2 e^{-x^2}\,dx = \frac{\sqrt{\pi}}{4}$, multiplying by $4$ gives $\sqrt{\pi}$. (D) $\int_{-\infty}^\infty x^2 e^{-x^2}\,dx = \frac{\sqrt{\pi}}{2} \neq \sqrt{\pi}$. Hence, options (A), (B), and (C) are correct.

questions.questionTextEn: Consider a monoatomic face-centered cubic (FCC) crystal of conventional lattice constant $a$ composed of identical touching hard spheres of radius $R$. Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?
optionsEn: The volume of the primitive unit cell is $\frac{a^3}{4}$
questions.explanationEn: For an FCC crystal: (A) Atoms touch along the face diagonal of length $\sqrt{2}a$, so $4R = \sqrt{2}a$ and the nearest-neighbor distance is $2R = \frac{a}{\sqrt{2}}$ (True). (B) Each atom has $12$ equidistant nearest neighbors (True). (C) There are $4$ atoms per conventional cell of volume $a^3$, so the primitive cell volume is $\frac{a^3}{4}$ (True). (D) The packing fraction of FCC is $\frac{\pi}{3\sqrt{2}} \approx 0.74$, whereas $\frac{\pi\sqrt{3}}{8} \approx 0.68$ is for BCC (False). Hence, options (A), (B), and (C) are correct.

questions.questionTextEn: Consider a classical ideal gas of $N$ non-linear triatomic molecules (such as $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ vapor) at temperature $T$. Which of the following statement(s) is/are TRUE?
optionsEn: When vibrational modes are completely frozen, the molar heat capacity is $C_V = 3R$
When vibrational modes are completely frozen, the adiabatic index is $\gamma = \frac{4}{3}$
A non-linear triatomic molecule has $3$ normal vibrational modes
When all vibrational modes are fully excited classically, $C_V = \frac{9}{2}R$
questions.explanationEn: A non-linear molecule with $n = 3$ atoms has $3$ translational, $3$ rotational, and $3n - 6 = 3$ vibrational modes (C True). With vibrations frozen, $f = 6 \implies C_V = 3R$ (A True) and $\gamma = 1 + 2/6 = 4/3$ (B True). With all $3$ vibrational modes classically excited (each contributing $R$ to $C_V$), $C_V = 3R + 3R = 6R \neq \frac{9}{2}R$ (D False). Hence, (A), (B), and (C) are correct.

questions.questionTextEn: Three non-interacting identical particles are placed in a 1D quantum harmonic oscillator with energy levels $E_n = \left(n + \frac{1}{2}\right)\hbar\omega$ ($n = 0, 1, 2, \dots$). Which of the following statement(s) is/are TRUE regarding the ground-state total energy $E_{\text{tot}}$ of the three-particle system?
optionsEn: If the particles are spin-$0$ bosons, $E_{\text{tot}} = \frac{3}{2}\hbar\omega$
If the particles are spin-$1/2$ fermions, $E_{\text{tot}} = \frac{5}{2}\hbar\omega$
If the particles are spinless (polarized) fermions, $E_{\text{tot}} = \frac{9}{2}\hbar\omega$
If the particles are spin-$1/2$ fermions, $E_{\text{tot}} = \frac{9}{2}\hbar\omega$
questions.explanationEn: (A) True: All $3$ bosons occupy $n = 0$, giving $3(\frac{1}{2}\hbar\omega) = \frac{3}{2}\hbar\omega$. (B) True: $2$ spin-$1/2$ fermions occupy $n = 0$ and $1$ occupies $n = 1$, giving $2(\frac{1}{2}) + 1(\frac{3}{2}) = \frac{5}{2}\hbar\omega$ (so D is False). (C) True: Spinless fermions occupy $n = 0, 1, 2$, giving $(\frac{1}{2} + \frac{3}{2} + \frac{5}{2})\hbar\omega = \frac{9}{2}\hbar\omega$. Hence, (A), (B), and (C) are correct.

questions.questionTextEn: Consider the $2 \times 2$ matrix $H = \begin{pmatrix} 3 & 2 - i \\ 2 + i & 3 \end{pmatrix}$. Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?
optionsEn: Both eigenvalues of $H$ are strictly positive
questions.explanationEn: (D) $H^\dagger = (H^*)^T = H$, so $H$ is Hermitian. (C) $\det(H) = 3(3) - (2 - i)(2 + i) = 9 - 5 = 4$. (A) The eigenvalues satisfy $\lambda^2 - 6\lambda + 4 = 0 \implies \lambda = 3 \pm \sqrt{5}$, both strictly positive since $3 > \sqrt{5} \approx 2.24$. (B) $H^\dagger H = H^2 \neq I$ (its determinant is $16 \neq 1$), so $H$ is not unitary. Hence, options (A), (C), and (D) are correct.

questions.questionTextEn: In a charge-free and current-free vacuum ($\rho = 0, \vec{J} = \vec{0}$), Maxwell's equations imply which of the following statements?
optionsEn: For a monochromatic plane wave with wavevector $\vec{k}$, $\vec{k}\cdot\vec{E} = 0$ and $\vec{k}\cdot\vec{B} = 0$
$\vec{E}$, $\vec{B}$, and $\vec{k}$ form a mutually orthogonal right-handed triad
The electric field $\vec{E}$ and magnetic field $\vec{B}$ of a plane wave in vacuum are $\frac{\pi}{2}$ out of phase with each other
Both $\vec{E}$ and $\vec{B}$ satisfy the homogeneous three-dimensional wave equation with speed $c = \frac{1}{\sqrt{\mu_0 \varepsilon_0}}$
questions.explanationEn: In free space, $\nabla^2\vec{E} = \mu_0\varepsilon_0\frac{\partial^2\vec{E}}{\partial t^2}$ (and similarly for $\vec{B}$), plane waves are strictly transverse ($\vec{k}\perp\vec{E}, \vec{k}\perp\vec{B}$), and $\vec{E}\times\vec{B}$ points along $\vec{k}$ (first three True). In vacuum, $\vec{E}$ and $\vec{B}$ oscillate in phase, not $\pi/2$ out of phase (False).

questions.questionTextEn: An ice cube containing a small embedded lead shot floats in a glass filled to the brim with water. Which of the following statement(s) is/are true as the ice completely melts (neglecting thermal expansion of water)?
optionsEn: After the ice melts, the lead shot sinks to the bottom of the glass
Water overflows from the glass as the ice melts
While floating, the ice-plus-lead system displaces a volume of water whose weight equals the combined weight of ice and lead
The water level in the glass drops after the ice completely melts
questions.explanationEn: While floating, the displaced water volume is $V_1 = \frac{m_{\text{ice}} + m_{\text{lead}}}{\rho_w}$ (A is true). After melting, the melted ice occupies $\frac{m_{\text{ice}}}{\rho_w}$ and the submerged lead shot (B is true) displaces only its own volume $\frac{m_{\text{lead}}}{\rho_{\text{lead}}} < \frac{m_{\text{lead}}}{\rho_w}$ (since $\rho_{\text{lead}} > \rho_w$). Thus total volume decreases and the water level drops (C is true, D is false). Hence, options (A), (C), and (D) are correct.

questions.questionTextEn: An inductor $L$ carrying an initial steady current $I_0$ is suddenly disconnected from its source and connected across a resistor $R$ at $t = 0$. Which of the following statements is/are correct?
optionsEn: The time constant of decay is $\tau = L/R$
The total thermal energy dissipated in the resistor from $t = 0$ to $t = \infty$ equals $\frac{1}{2}L I_0^2$
At $t = \tau$, the magnetic energy remaining in the inductor is $\frac{1}{e}$ of its initial value
The current decays exponentially as $I(t) = I_0 e^{-Rt/L}$
questions.explanationEn: Solving $L\frac{dI}{dt} + IR = 0$ gives $I(t) = I_0 e^{-t/\tau}$ with $\tau = L/R$, and $\int_0^\infty I^2 R\,dt = \frac{1}{2}LI_0^2$ (first three True). Since $U_B(t) = \frac{1}{2}L I(t)^2 = U_0 e^{-2t/\tau}$, at $t = \tau$ the remaining energy is $U_0 e^{-2}$, not $U_0 e^{-1}$ (False).

questions.questionTextEn: A lightly damped harmonic oscillator ($\gamma \ll \omega_0$) is driven by a sinusoidal force $F(t) = F_0\cos(\omega t)$. In the steady state, which of the following statements is/are correct?
optionsEn: For $\omega \gg \omega_0$, the displacement lags the driving force by nearly $\pi$
At $\omega = \omega_0$, the steady-state displacement amplitude is independent of the damping parameter $\gamma$
The full width at half maximum (FWHM) of the power resonance curve $\langle P(\omega) \rangle$ is $\Delta\omega = 2\gamma$
For $\omega \ll \omega_0$, the displacement is nearly in phase with the driving force and has amplitude $\approx \frac{F_0}{m\omega_0^2}$
questions.explanationEn: At low frequency ($\omega \ll \omega_0$), stiffness dominates: $x_0 \approx F_0/(m\omega_0^2)$ and $\delta \to 0$ (True). At high frequency ($\omega \gg \omega_0$), inertia dominates: $\delta \to \pi$ (True). The power resonance curve has FWHM $\Delta\omega = 2\gamma = \omega_0/Q$ (True). At $\omega = \omega_0$, $x_0 = F_0/(2m\gamma\omega_0)$, which depends inversely on $\gamma$ (False).

questions.questionTextEn: Consider two events $E_1$ and $E_2$ with Minkowski interval $\Delta s^2 = (c\Delta t)^2 - |\Delta \vec{r}|^2$. Which of the following statement(s) is/are TRUE?
optionsEn: If $\Delta s^2 > 0$ (time-like), the temporal order of $E_1$ and $E_2$ is the same in all inertial frames
If $\Delta s^2 > 0$, there exists an inertial frame in which $E_1$ and $E_2$ occur at the same spatial location
If $\Delta s^2 < 0$ (space-like), the two events cannot be causally connected by any signal traveling at or below speed $c$
If $\Delta s^2 = 0$ (light-like), there exists an inertial frame in which $E_1$ and $E_2$ occur simultaneously at different locations
questions.explanationEn: (A) True: Time-like separated events have invariant causal/temporal ordering. (B) True: Moving at $v = \Delta x / \Delta t < c$ brings both events to the same spatial point. (C) True: Space-like separation means $|\Delta \vec{r}| > c|\Delta t|$, outside the light cone. (D) False: For $\Delta s^2 = 0$, $\Delta t' = 0$ would force $|\Delta \vec{r}'| = 0$ (same event). Hence, (A), (B), and (C) are correct.

questions.questionTextEn: In the Maclaurin series expansion of $\cos(2x)$, the coefficient of $x^4$ is ____. (Rounded off to two decimal places)
questions.explanationEn: Since $\cos u = 1 - \frac{u^2}{2!} + \frac{u^4}{4!} - \cdots$, substituting $u = 2x$ gives the $x^4$ coefficient as $\frac{2^4}{24} = \frac{16}{24} = \frac{2}{3} \approx 0.67$.

questions.questionTextEn: In the truth table of the $3$-variable Boolean function $Y(A, B, C) = A + B\bar{C}$, the total number of input combinations for which $Y = 1$ is ______. (Answer in integer)
questions.explanationEn: Out of $2^3 = 8$ input combinations $(A, B, C)$: $A = 1$ accounts for $4$ combinations ($100, 101, 110, 111$). When $A = 0$, $B\bar{C} = 1$ only for $(0, 1, 0)$, adding $1$ more combination. Thus, $Y = 1$ for $4 + 1 = 5$ input combinations.

questions.questionTextEn: An X-ray tube operates at an accelerating potential of $25\text{ kV}$. Taking $hc = 1240\text{ eV}\cdot\text{nm}$, the shortest wavelength of X-rays emitted is ______ $\text{\AA}$ (Round off to 2 decimal places).
questions.explanationEn: The cutoff wavelength is $\lambda_{\min} = \frac{hc}{eV} = \frac{1240\text{ eV}\cdot\text{nm}}{25000\text{ eV}} = 0.0496\text{ nm} = 0.496\text{ \AA} \approx 0.50\text{ \AA}$.

questions.questionTextEn: A long air-core solenoid has $2000\text{ turns/m}$ and carries a steady current of $5\text{ A}$. Taking $\mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7}\text{ T}\cdot\text{m/A}$, the magnetic field inside the solenoid near its center is ______ $\text{mT}$. (Round off to 2 decimal places)
questions.explanationEn: Inside a long solenoid, $B = \mu_0 n I = (4\pi \times 10^{-7})(2000)(5) = 4\pi \times 10^{-3}\text{ T} \approx 12.57\text{ mT}$.

questions.questionTextEn: The angle (in degrees) between the vectors $\vec{A} = \hat{i} + \hat{j}$ and $\vec{B} = \hat{j} + \hat{k}$ is ____. (Answer in integer)
questions.explanationEn: $\cos\theta = \frac{\vec{A}\cdot\vec{B}}{|\vec{A}||\vec{B}|} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}\cdot\sqrt{2}} = \frac{1}{2}$, so $\theta = 60^\circ$.

questions.questionTextEn: Taking Wien's displacement constant as $2.90 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}\cdot\text{K}$, the wavelength of peak spectral emission for a blackbody at temperature $5800\text{ K}$ is ______ $\text{nm}$ (Answer in integer).
questions.explanationEn: By Wien's displacement law, $\lambda_{\max} = \frac{2.90 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}\cdot\text{K}}{5800\text{ K}} = 5.0 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m} = 500\text{ nm}$.

questions.questionTextEn: A straight metal rod of length $0.5\text{ m}$ moves at a constant speed of $8\text{ m/s}$ perpendicular to both its own length and a uniform magnetic field of $0.25\text{ T}$. The motional emf induced across the ends of the rod is ______ $\text{V}$. (Answer in integer)
questions.explanationEn: The motional emf is $\mathcal{E} = BLv = 0.25 \times 0.5 \times 8 = 1\text{ V}$.

questions.questionTextEn: An asteroid orbits the Sun in an elliptical orbit with a semi-major axis of $4\text{ AU}$. Given that the Earth's orbital semi-major axis is $1\text{ AU}$ with a period of $1\text{ year}$, the orbital period of the asteroid, in years, is ____. (Answer in integer)
questions.explanationEn: By Kepler's third law, $T = \left(\frac{a}{1\text{ AU}}\right)^{3/2}\text{ yr} = 4^{3/2} = 8\text{ years}$.

questions.questionTextEn: A guitar string of length $0.5\text{ m}$ and linear mass density $5\text{ g/m}$ is stretched to a tension of $50\text{ N}$. Its fundamental frequency of vibration is ______ $\text{Hz}$. (Answer in integer)
questions.explanationEn: The wave speed is $v = \sqrt{\frac{T}{\mu}} = \sqrt{\frac{50}{0.005}} = 100\text{ m/s}$. The fundamental frequency is $f_1 = \frac{v}{2L} = \frac{100}{2 \times 0.5} = 100\text{ Hz}$.

questions.questionTextEn: One mole of neon and one mole of krypton, initially at the same temperature and pressure in equal volumes, are allowed to mix adiabatically. Taking $R = 8.314\text{ J/(mol}\cdot\text{K)}$, the total entropy of mixing is ______ $\text{J/K}$ (Round off to 2 decimal places).
questions.explanationEn: The entropy of mixing is $\Delta S = n_1 R \ln 2 + n_2 R \ln 2 = 2R\ln 2 = 2 \times 8.314 \times 0.69315 \approx 11.53\text{ J/K}$.

questions.questionTextEn: Electrons with kinetic energy $1.0\text{ eV}$ are incident on a 1D rectangular potential barrier of height $5.0\text{ eV}$ and width $0.50\text{ nm}$. In the WKB/thick-barrier approximation $T \approx \frac{16E(V_0 - E)}{V_0^2}e^{-\eta}$, using $m_e = 9.11 \times 10^{-31}\text{ kg}$, $\hbar = 1.055 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J}\cdot\text{s}$, and $1\text{ eV} = 1.602 \times 10^{-19}\text{ J}$, the dimensionless exponent $\eta = 2\kappa a$ is ______ (Round off to 2 decimal places).
questions.explanationEn: The decay constant is $\kappa = \frac{\sqrt{2m_e(V_0 - E)}}{\hbar} = \frac{\sqrt{2(9.11 \times 10^{-31})(4 \times 1.602 \times 10^{-19})}}{1.055 \times 10^{-34}} \approx 1.0244 \times 10^{10}\text{ m}^{-1}$. Thus $\eta = 2\kappa a = 2(1.0244 \times 10^{10})(0.50 \times 10^{-9}) \approx 10.24$.

questions.questionTextEn: In a spherically symmetric region, the electrostatic field is given by $\vec{E}(r) = 5r^3\hat{r}\text{ V/m}$ (with $r$ in meters). The total electric charge enclosed within a sphere of radius $R = 2\text{ m}$ centered at the origin is ______ $\pi\varepsilon_0\text{ C}$. (Answer in integer)
questions.explanationEn: By Gauss's law, $Q_{\text{enc}} = \varepsilon_0 \oint \vec{E}\cdot d\vec{S} = \varepsilon_0 (5R^3)(4\pi R^2) = 20\pi\varepsilon_0 R^5$. At $R = 2\text{ m}$, $Q_{\text{enc}} = 20(32)\pi\varepsilon_0 = 640\pi\varepsilon_0\text{ C}$.

questions.questionTextEn: A quantum particle is described by the normalized Gaussian wavefunction $\psi(x) = \left(\frac{1}{\pi a^2}\right)^{1/4} e^{-x^2 / (2a^2)}$ ($a > 0$). The expectation value $\langle \hat{p}_x^2 \rangle$ is $\alpha \frac{\hbar^2}{a^2}$, where $\alpha$ is ______ (Round off to 2 decimal places).
questions.explanationEn: Since $\psi(x)$ is the ground state of a harmonic oscillator with $\Delta x = \frac{a}{\sqrt{2}}$ and $\Delta x\,\Delta p_x = \frac{\hbar}{2}$ (and $\langle p_x \rangle = 0$), we get $\Delta p_x = \frac{\hbar}{\sqrt{2}\,a}$, so $\langle \hat{p}_x^2 \rangle = (\Delta p_x)^2 = \frac{\hbar^2}{2a^2} = 0.50\frac{\hbar^2}{a^2}$.

questions.questionTextEn: Two DC cells—one of emf $12\text{ V}$ with internal resistance $2\ \Omega$ and another of emf $6\text{ V}$ with internal resistance $4\ \Omega$—are connected in parallel (positive terminals together, negative terminals together) across a $4\ \Omega$ external load resistor. The terminal voltage across the $4\ \Omega$ load resistor is ______ $\text{V}$. (Round off to 1 decimal place)
questions.explanationEn: Applying Kirchhoff's current law at the positive node (voltage $V$): $\frac{V - 12}{2} + \frac{V - 6}{4} + \frac{V}{4} = 0 \implies 2(V - 12) + (V - 6) + V = 0 \implies 4V = 30 \implies V = 7.5\text{ V}$.

questions.questionTextEn: The maximum value of $f(x, y) = 4x + 3y$ subject to the constraint $x^2 + y^2 = 25$ is ____. (Answer in integer)
questions.explanationEn: By the method of Lagrange multipliers (or Cauchy–Schwarz inequality), $\nabla f = \lambda \nabla g \implies (4, 3) = \lambda(2x, 2y)$, so $x = \frac{2}{\lambda}$ and $y = \frac{3}{2\lambda}$. Substituting into $x^2 + y^2 = 25$ gives $\frac{25}{4\lambda^2} = 25 \implies \lambda = \pm\frac{1}{2}$, yielding the maximum at $(4, 3)$ with $f(4, 3) = 16 + 9 = 25$.

questions.questionTextEn: In a positional number system of integer base $r$, the multiplication $(34)_r \times (2)_r = (101)_r$ is valid. The value of the base $r$ is ______. (Answer in integer)
questions.explanationEn: Convert to base $10$: $(3r + 4) \times 2 = 1 \cdot r^2 + 0 \cdot r + 1 \implies 6r + 8 = r^2 + 1 \implies r^2 - 6r - 7 = 0 \implies (r - 7)(r + 1) = 0$. Since the base $r$ must be a positive integer greater than all digits ($> 4$), we obtain $r = 7$.

questions.questionTextEn: A Fresnel zone plate is designed to have a primary focal length of $50\text{ cm}$ for monochromatic light of wavelength $500\text{ nm}$. The radius of the first half-period zone is ______ $\text{mm}$. (Round off to 2 decimal places)
questions.explanationEn: The primary focal length of a zone plate is $f_1 = \frac{r_1^2}{\lambda}$, so $r_1 = \sqrt{f_1 \lambda} = \sqrt{0.50 \times 500 \times 10^{-9}} = 5.0 \times 10^{-4}\text{ m} = 0.50\text{ mm}$.

questions.questionTextEn: A bullet of mass $20\text{ g}$ traveling horizontally at $300\text{ m/s}$ strikes and embeds itself in a stationary wooden block of mass $1.98\text{ kg}$ suspended as a ballistic pendulum. Taking $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$, the maximum vertical height risen by the block-bullet system, in $\text{cm}$, is ____. (Answer in integer)
questions.explanationEn: By momentum conservation during the impact, $v_f = \frac{mv}{m + M} = \frac{0.02 \times 300}{0.02 + 1.98} = 3\text{ m/s}$. By energy conservation during the swing, $h = \frac{v_f^2}{2g} = \frac{9}{20} = 0.45\text{ m} = 45\text{ cm}$.

questions.questionTextEn: A body of constant heat capacity $500\text{ J/K}$ at $600\text{ K}$ is placed in thermal contact with another body of constant heat capacity $1000\text{ J/K}$ at $300\text{ K}$ inside an insulated enclosure. The total entropy change of the combined system upon reaching equilibrium is ______ $\text{J/K}$ (Round off to 2 decimal places).
questions.explanationEn: Energy conservation gives $T_f = \frac{500(600) + 1000(300)}{500 + 1000} = 400\text{ K}$. The total entropy change is $\Delta S = 500\ln\left(\frac{400}{600}\right) + 1000\ln\left(\frac{400}{300}\right) = -202.73 + 287.68 = 84.95\text{ J/K}$.

questions.questionTextEn: The value of the double integral $\int_0^\infty \int_0^\infty e^{-(x^2 + y^2)/4}\,dx\,dy$ is ____. (Rounded off to two decimal places)
questions.explanationEn: Converting to polar coordinates over the first quadrant ($0 \le r < \infty$, $0 \le \theta \le \frac{\pi}{2}$): $I = \int_0^{\pi/2} d\theta \int_0^\infty e^{-r^2/4} r\,dr = \frac{\pi}{2}\left[-2e^{-r^2/4}\right]_0^\infty = \frac{\pi}{2}(2) = \pi \approx 3.14$.
